title: The Mézard–Parisi formula for diluted spin glasses
main_claim: For Poisson diluted even-p Ising models in the Panchenko–Talagrand class (factorized e^θ = a(1+bΠf_ℓ), E(-b)^n ≥ 0), assuming only E B(θ)+E|h| < ∞, lim F_N exists and equals inf_r Φ_r, the infimum of the finite-level hierarchical (Mézard–Parisi / Panchenko–Talagrand) trial functional. The lower bound is claimed for any bounded permutation-invariant interaction, with no factorization or positivity needed.
coverage:
I read all of the LaTeX sections and checked these by hand.
- Upper bound (§upper): the degenerate-factorization bounds on b and M; the λ-regularization convex-combination identity; how the log-expansion coefficient becomes -λ^n/n E(-b)^n E_Q[P^p - pPB^{p-1} + (p-1)B^p]; the sign, via convexity of x^p for even p.
- Tree calculus (§trees): the insertion density exponents γ_β; telescoping; the Q_k normalization; the k-th derivative coefficient (-1)^{k-1}(k-1)!; the canceled-anchor rule; the worked two-path example m_d - m_{d+1}; the reference-total lemma (m_d - j m_{d+1}); charging bounds; regular-shape probabilities.
- Cavity increment (§cavity): the Poisson splitting means ρ_N and α(p-1); the perturbation coupling error O(N^{-1/4}).
- Perturbations (§pert): the second-derivative/variance formula with m_L = 1; the thermal and convex-derivative concentration rates (N^{1/2}/ρ vs λ = N^{3/4}, ρ = N^{-1/8}); the Mecke/Palm cancellation of the anchor factor; the analytic argument that H ≡ 0 (j^{-j} vs j^{-q}); the polarization constant k^k/(2^k k!); the mark selectors H_d - H_{d+1}.
- Decorrelation (§decor), checked in detail:
  - the one-leaf identity: Σc_ℓ = 1+δ, giving δ·Var + o(1);
  - the shifted two-copy class coefficients -c_d J, -δJ and m_e J, which reconcile with the total -δJ;
  - the replacement f → a·b, using equal marginals of a·b and a·b_ℓ;
  - the three-copy trace bound and the fiber/Hölder averaging behind the recursion V_k ≤ C(L^{-1/2} + V_{k-1}^{1/4});
  - the marker-anchor step Var(M) → 0 with coefficient -δκ(S) ≠ 0.
- Comparison (§comp): the encoding x = arctanh⟨σ_i⟩ and the backward conditional laws; the TV pattern bound; Q_k-to-average conversion; factorization of the bond term giving α(p-1)E log T_0V_e; the order of limits M, q, N, L.
- Reduction: the shift identity (-αp + α(p-1) = -α) and the truncation/stability bounds.

I found no step that fails. I did not check the zero-temperature corollaries in §consequences beyond the hypothesis checks for Viana–Bray and SAT. No sympy computations were needed because the algebra is short and I verified it by hand.
